messages:
maria: FYI customer on Dedicated is blocked building their service after we pushed the new v2 tagged release of the Go client. go get fails with a module path mismatch error.

maria: Error they see:```
verifying github.com/redwood-inference/go-client@v2.1.0: checksum mismatch
module declares its path as: github.com/redwood-inference/go-client/v2
but was required as: github.com/redwood-inference/go-client
```

devon: ugh, classic v2-modpath mismatch. Did they use the v2 import path in their code (i.e. import "github.com/redwood-inference/go-client/v2")?

maria: They said their repo imports the non-/v2 path (legacy), but their go.mod requires github.com/redwood-inference/go-client v1.0.0 earlier. After we published v2.1.0 the proxy seems to resolve the tag but then the module path in the zip is the /v2 path, so go complains.

sre_jamie: Can you paste their go env and the exact go get output? sometimes GOPROXY or use of a private proxy causes weirdness.

maria: They shared this:```
GO111MODULE=on
GOPROXY=https://proxy.golang.org,direct
GOSUMDB=sum.golang.org

$ go get github.com/redwood-inference/go-client@v2.1.0
go: github.com/redwood-inference/go-client@v2.1.0: reading github.com/redwood-inference/go-client/go.mod at revision v2.1.0: unknown revision v2.1.0
(or sometimes) module declares its path as github.com/redwood-inference/go-client/v2
```

eng-ryan: Two likely causes: our tag naming or the module's go.mod module path. For v2+ modules you must both: (1) set module path to include /v2 in go.mod and (2) tag releases using semver with the v2.x.x tag. If either is wrong, clients get a mismatch.

devon: pkg-bot published the release on Friday — did our release job ensure go.mod module path contains /v2? pkg-bot, can you confirm the release artifact contents? :eyes:

pkg-bot: release 2026-03-13/v2.1.0 published to releases.redwood.ci. Artifacts: zip, source. Checking go.mod in tag v2.1.0... found module github.com/redwood-inference/go-client (NO /v2).

maria: there we go. The zip's go.mod is still the v1 path. That will cause 'module declares its path as github.com/redwood-inference/go-client' while we expected /v2, so consumers doing import ".../v2" see mismatch, and those importing without /v2 hit unknown revision.

sre_jamie: Short term workarounds for the customer:
- Have them import the v2 path explicitly (import "github.com/redwood-inference/go-client/v2") and use `go get github.com/redwood-inference/go-client/v2@v2.1.0`
- Or add a temporary replace in their go.mod pointing the old path to the v2 module zip (not ideal).

eng-ryan: Longer term fix: we need to re-tag properly and cut a patched release. Steps for release owner: update module path to include /v2 in go.mod, commit, tag v2.1.1 (or v3 if major bump) and publish. Also update release pipeline to validate module path vs tag before publishing.

devon: Also check customers who vendor or use a private GOPROXY — they might have cached the bad artifact. We'll need to invalidate or force-publish the corrected tag.

maria: Customer accepts workaround for now but asked for ETA. Can we target a patched release within today?

pkg-bot: CI preflight: running go list -m -json ./... on the tag, verifying module path; currently failing on v2.1.0. Triggered manual release run.

eng-ryan: I'll patch the module and cut v2.1.1 in ~2 hours. I'll also add a CI job to assert that the module path has the major /vN suffix when tag >= v2.0.0.

devon: Thanks. Please post back with the new tag so I can relay to the customer and close the ticket. :thumbsup:

maria: Noted. I'll update support ticket with the workaround steps and mark as escalated to eng.

sre_jamie: Reminder for docs: add a short note to the Go client release checklist about the module path rule and how to avoid consumers' build breaks.

maria: Will do. Closing loop when v2.1.1 is live.
